Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National | Top Story Supreme Court, Court of Appeal to go fully digital from January 2027 – Chief Justice Source : Myjoyonline.com 28 November 2026 9:57am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal will begin full electronic filing, authentication, service and related court processes from January 2, 2027, Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie has announced.
The rollout forms part of the Judiciary’s E-Justice Plus Programme, which is being introduced in phases, with the High Court expected to be brought on board from July 2, 2027.
The Chief Justice made the announcement at the launch of the programme in Accra, describing it as the next phase of efforts to automate court processes and improve the administration of justice in Ghana.
The Judicial Service began piloting the system on November 22, 2026, as part of efforts to automate manual processes within court registries and address challenges such as missing case dockets.
The original E-Justice programme was designed to cover the entire life cycle of a case, from filing to the execution of court decisions.
“The roll-out to the High Court will follow on July 2, 2027. This phased approach is intended to ensure that the transition is properly managed and the necessary institutional and technical support is in place at each stage,” the Chief Justice said.
He said E-Justice Plus would expand paperless court processes to the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal, strengthening electronic filing and service, improving the management of judicial records and making court services more accessible.
“It is part of the broader commitment to automate court processes, strengthen electronic filing and service, improve the management of judicial records and make the work of the courts more accessible to those who use them,” he said.
Justice Baffoe-Bonnie said the programme had moved from the pilot stage into preparations for practical use, with the initial testing expected to help the Judiciary and court users identify and resolve challenges before full implementation.
“The pilot will allow the Judiciary and its users to test the processes, identify any difficulties and address them before full implementation,” he said.
He said a properly functioning digital system should enable documents to be filed and received electronically, court fees to be assessed and paid through secure electronic channels, and case records to be retrieved more easily.
It is also expected to allow authorised users to track the progress of their cases without making unnecessary visits to court registries.
The Chief Justice said the system would improve the organisation of court business and support judges and registry officers while strengthening the reliability of records on which judicial decisions depend.
He added that the programme would facilitate electronic case filing, digital management and preservation of court records, electronic payments and the use of electronic signatures.
Justice Baffoe-Bonnie, however, stressed that the introduction of virtual proceedings did not diminish the importance of the courtroom.
He urged judges, lawyers, judicial staff and court users to embrace the programme and familiarise themselves with its operations.
Justice Jennifer Abena Dadzie, who represented the Chairman of the Change Management Committee, urged stakeholders to approach the transition positively and regard E-Justice Plus as a shared institutional responsibility.
The Judicial Secretary, Musah Ahmed, said the E-Justice system had been developed as a paperless case management platform to support the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal by bringing case information, documents and related processes into a centralised digital environment.
He said the Judicial Service was committed to ensuring that the system remained accessible to people with limited internet access, those unfamiliar with digital services and persons with disabilities who might require assistance.
“This internal go-live and demonstration provide an opportunity for our justices and other stakeholders to become familiar with the system, appreciate its functions, and understand how it is expected to support their respective roles.
“It is also an opportunity to identify areas requiring further attention as we work towards a phased, effective implementation,” Mr Ahmed said.
